Stage 07, step 3 · batch 3 of 3, organisms

Kit of components

The classes every screen in colour will be assembled from, in design/kit/kit.css. Read from the code of Home v4 and the case screen v4, and, for what is still only grey, from the wireframes' structure and DESIGN.md's language. Batch 1 is the 24 atoms, batch 2 the 21 molecules built from them, batch 3 the 22 organisms that hold them, the shell among them: the rail, the header, the footer, the bottom bar and the ticker. Since D-229 the kit holds only the language of Home v4 and the case screen v4: direction 2's values and art live in design/archive/theme-d2.css for the pages that record it.

Atoms

Each is one class with its variants as modifiers. Values come only from the variables in Tokens below; no class carries a value of its own.

Button

One family. Size is set by the container: large 52, medium 40, small 32, at every width (D-228). Primary is the one filled act of its zone; ghost is the second act; icon and close are the square controls.

Organisms

Each holds molecules and atoms from above, and an organism comes after every organism it holds. Those Home v4 and the case screen v4 draw were carried over from the rules that draw them and compared with their originals at 1440 and 360; those still only grey are built from their nearest relative in colour, named in each block's heading in kit.css (D-232). Where an organism needs another form of a component it holds, that form is a modifier in the component's own block. The shell is shown in frames: a slice of the page beside the rail, and phones of 360px.

Account head

Who this account is, over the four account pages: the breadcrumb, the picture, the name, the ID a person reads out to support and the Steam account the items go to, the money pair with Add funds, and the four tabs. Grey only so far; built from its nearest relative in colour, the head of the account's menu in the header, on the header strip's plate. After My items' gate (D-240) a band in the Cases mode's pink to violet under its stripes, the operators of the footer rising over its right end from 1200px, the picture at 88px, the ID and the Steam account as chips, the money pair at a price's size and Add funds, the filled act with the header's 5% pin, on one dark plate as the header's, and the tabs on the plate under the band, each with its mark. After its second gate (D-241), on My items, the most valuable item held takes the operators' place from 1200px: its skin large and turned over the band's right end, breathing and breaking out over its top, on its hexagon in its grade, its name huge and dark behind it, and a chip saying Highest value, the gun and skin, its value; items.js reads it from the grid, so it follows a sale, and with nothing readable held the operators return. After its third look (D-242), the founder's pick B1 from the head's lab (design/v4/myitems-lab.html): on My items the head takes its stage form at every width, the band dark at the left and in the best item's grade at the right, the name in heavy italic capitals over the money plate, the skin with no plinth coming out over the band's top with a contact shadow under it and the outcome card's foil running across it, its name in capitals behind it, the Highest value chip over it; a pistol drawn smaller than a rifle; on a phone the skin first. With nothing readable held the band is pink again and the operators stand in the skin's place.

What opening a case here involves

Home: the paragraph whole under its head, Nightfall on its striped plate with three quotes. Even columns under 1000px of its width, one under 720px, the quotes inside the plate under 560px.

What opening a case here involves

A case is a fixed set of CS2 skins with a published chance on each one. You pay its price in coins, one round decides the item, and you can keep it, sell it or send it to your Steam inventory. Every case shows its chances, its item values and its tested return before you open it, and every round can be checked afterwards.

About Clutch

Home: a lead, then four short parts under their heads in two columns, parted by hairlines; one column under 600px of its width.

About Clutch

Clutch is a CS2 case opening site built so that its own numbers can be checked. Every case shows the chance of each skin, its value and its tested return before you spend, and every round leaves a proof you can recompute.

CS2 cases with published odds

Each case is a fixed set of CS2 skins. Its page lists every item with its chance and its current value, so you see what a case pays before you open it, not after.

Provably fair rounds

Every round leaves a proof. You can recompute it yourself, without an account, on the Provably fair page, and a round that does not match is something you can show us.

Skins you can send to Steam

An item from a case waits in My items until you choose: keep it, sell it for coins or send it to your Steam inventory. You sign in on Steam's own page, and we never ask for your password.

Play with limits

Clutch is for people 18 or over. Deposit limits, session limits, a cool down and self exclusion are on the Responsible play page, and no limit ever stops you sending items to Steam.

How this case works

The case screen: the prose on its plate beside the ticket ruler, the 100 000 tickets as a line of items as wide as their chances; the pin runs to the ticket and the item it falls in shows under the tear, played once in view. One column under 900px.

How this case works

The price buys one round, and the round lands on one item. Every item's chance is printed as a percentage and as a ticket range: the range is what the round resolves against, which is what makes a result checkable.

How a round is checked

The round is fixed before the animation starts and its hash is on screen when you open. After the reveal, one link checks the round against that hash.

What this proves

The result of this round was fixed before you clicked, and it was not changed afterwards.

What this does not prove

That the chances we publish are the chances the round used.

What a round proof is made of

What a round proof is made of

Server seed hash
Published before the round runs
Server seed
Revealed on rotation
Client seed
Shown with every round
Nonce
A whole number that advances
Settled result
The number the round produced
Ticket range
The interval the result falls in, and the item holding it
The drop table in force at that round, versioned
Its version, printed with the round

The algorithm, published in full

Provably fair: on the prose plate of How this case works, its version on a status Badge beside the head, the computation and its history beside the worked example and its two links, a seed or a ticket in the hash well's dark chip. One column under 900px.

The algorithm, published in full

Version 1, published 12 Jan 2026

The computation

HMAC-SHA256 of the server seed, keyed with client seed:nonce. The first eight hex characters, read as a number, modulo 100 000, plus one, is the ticket. The item whose ticket range holds it is the result.

Version history

Version 1, 12 Jan 2026. First published.

A worked example

Server seed 7c1e…a904, client seed nightjar, nonce 412. HMAC starts 3a9009c1, which is 982 518 209; modulo 100 000 plus one is ticket 18 210, in the range 11 001 to 23 000, USP-S Kill Confirmed.

Check this roundIts public page

Motion

The motion v4 Home was approved with, carried into the kit whole by D-235 so that every screen built from it moves as v4 does. Its rules are in kit.css beside the component they move, its behaviour in motion.js; for whoever asked for less motion everything here stands still. Also carried and seen in place above: the Disclosure slides open and shut and its plus turns to a minus, the Favourite bursts when it turns on, the Event banner counts down to its published end, the Ticker paces its arrivals, the row slides to make room, and a block off the screen pauses its loops.

Icon story

A mark of the rail, the footer's counters and its round plate, redrawn in parts so it can play the thing its row promises, in about a second, under the pointer or the keyboard's focus: a case opens, swords clash, a scope locks, a coin is tossed. Founder of 1 and 3 Nov 2026. Point at one.

One job, several forms: the six that clash

  • add funds: wf-ah-add in the account head and plain wf-btn in an empty state; the header's + carries the same job under a third class, wf-dep
  • check this round: one act on one object, a round: a small button on ledger and shelf cards, a text link under the outcome and on Provably fair
  • sell for #coins: the sell act carries three classes: wf-sell on a batch card, plain wf-btn primary in the single outcome's act row (D-140), plain wf-btn on 5.3. Rank by zone stands; the class does not
  • share this round: a small button on an item card and a text link under the outcome
  • sign out: a link-like row in the account menu and a button in Settings
  • support: the footer names Support twice in two forms, a link in its list and a button in its help cell; elsewhere it is a route button or an inline link, which is by zone

Control without a family

  • None in the product. The 133 unassigned controls are the wireframe panel's own toggle, a tool of the grey prototype.

Visuals

The product's own images, design/visuals/, 42 files chosen by the photo column above: 38 generated by Codex on gpt-5.6-terra, three drawn in code, one composed from two Codex images. One colourway: everything that is light, ground or a person is the brand's night, navy lit in pink and blue; a thing carries its own colour only on itself, a case its theme, a tier its metal, a mode its card's colour. Each file, its component, its variable and the prompt that made it are in design/visuals/README.md.

Cases Case tile, Case grid, Case head, Case stage

Daily tiers Daily ladder

Modes Mode card, Mode row

Event banner Event banner, in layers

Brand art Footer, the sign in dialog, the page ground, the header

Rare marks Drop card, Item card, Feed tile; strips of 24 frames drawn in code

Avatars Avatar, Account head, the account menu

The prompt the shared block, first in every new prompt; the prompt of each file follows it in the README

Original game key art for Clutch, a CS2 case-opening site. Premium PBR game render, believable matte physical materials, restrained lighting, crisp readable silhouette.
Palette: the brand's night. Ground #060A1E, light in hot pink #FB3F8A and electric blue #65A3FF. A thing carries its own colour only on itself: a case its theme, a Daily tier its metal, a mode its card colour.
Background: a cut-out object stands on uniform flat pure chroma green #00FF00, no shadow, glow, gradient or green spill on the object; a light layer (glow, burst, aurora) stands on uniform pure black #000000 for screen blend.
Edits: when an input image is given it is the edit target, not a style hint; preserve its camera, silhouette, proportions and framing, change only what is named.
Constraints: no text unless an exact stencil word is asked for; no logos, watermark, UI; no real people or known game characters; no weapon skins.
